Internal per-callsite record used by VLOG_IS_ON to cache and link verbosity control data. objects.definition:
enum LogSeverity {
  GLOG_INFO = 0,
  GLOG_WARNING = 1,
  GLOG_ERROR = 2,
  GLOG_FATAL = 3,
#ifndef GLOG_NO_ABBREVIATED_SEVERITIES
#  ifdef ERROR
#  error ERROR macro is defined. Define GLOG_NO_ABBREVIATED_SEVERITIES before including logging.h. See the document for detail.
#  endif
  INFO = GLOG_INFO,
  WARNING = GLOG_WARNING,
  ERROR = GLOG_ERROR,
  FATAL = GLOG_FATAL
#endif
};
objects.description: Enumeration of log severities used by google logging. Values are contiguous 0..3 and widely assumed to lie in [0, NUM_SEVERITIES-1]. Provides both GLOG_* names and, unless disabled, abbreviated aliases INFO/WARNING/ERROR/FATAL that map to the same underlying values.

constexpr int NUM_SEVERITIES = 4;
objects.description: Constant count of defined log severities. Used to bound valid LogSeverity values. Inline constexpr variable when supported.

enum { DEBUG_MODE = 0 };
#  define IF_DEBUG_MODE(x)
#else
enum { DEBUG_MODE = 1 };

#endif

Enables lightweight conditional compilation such as if (DEBUG_MODE) {...}. Note: Defined via an unnamed enum; treated here as an int-typed constant.

functions.description: Streams the contents of a std::vector to an ostream for logging-style output. Elements are written in sequence order, separated by a single space. Only the first 100 elements are printed; if more remain, " ..." is appended. Intended for logging/debug output.
requirements: Elements of the vector (type T1) must themselves be streamable to std::ostream via operator<<.
The provided std::ostream reference must be valid for output.
The vector must be in a valid state such that begin() and end() produce a valid range.

functions.name: google::PrintSequence

inline void google::PrintSequence(std::ostream& out, Iter begin, Iter end)
functions.description: Helper that streams a sequence delimited by [begin, end) to an ostream. Writes at most 100 space-separated elements by repeatedly applying operator<< to *begin and incrementing; appends " ..." if more elements remain. Used by the overloads that stream STL containers. Intended for logging only.
requirements: Iter must denote a valid input-range: repeatedly incrementable from begin toward end without undefined behavior.
Dereferencing Iter (i.e., *it) must yield a value that is streamable to std::ostream via operator<<.
The [begin, end) range must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: google::RawLog__
functions.signature: GLOG_EXPORT void google::RawLog__(LogSeverity severity, const char* file, int line, const char* format, ...);
functions.description: Low-level, thread-safe logger that writes a single printf-style formatted message directly to stderr without allocating memory or acquiring locks. Intended for use by low-level components that cannot use higher-level logging. Typically invoked via macros (RAW_LOG, RAW_VLOG) which supply file and line; can also be called directly. Very long messages may be silently truncated. The format string follows printf semantics and is compile-time checked on supported compilers.
requirements: severity must be a valid LogSeverity value (e.g., google::GLOG_INFO, google::GLOG_WARNING, google::GLOG_ERROR, google::GLOG_FATAL).
file must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string identifying the source file (typically __FILE__).
line should be a non-negative integer corresponding to the source line (typically __LINE__).
format must be a non-null, NUL-terminated printf-style format string.
The variadic arguments must exactly match the format string’s specifiers (printf rules); otherwise behavior is undefined.
Caller should not expect any buffering or memory allocation; output is written directly to stderr.
On compilers honoring __attribute__((format(printf,...))), mismatches between format and arguments will be diagnosed at compile time; callers must resolve such diagnostics.

functions.name: google::RawLogStub__
functions.description: No-op stub used to suppress unused-variable warnings when logging is compiled out (e.g., with STRIP_LOG > 0). Accepts any arguments and performs no formatting or I/O. Intended to be called via macros when logging is disabled.
requirements: No operational requirements; all parameters are ignored.
May be called with any values; has no side effects and returns immediately.

functions.name: google::SetVLOGLevel
functions.signature: extern GLOG_EXPORT int SetVLOGLevel(const char* module_pattern, int log_level);
functions.description: Sets the VLOG/VLOG_IS_ON level for modules matching module_pattern, providing limited dynamic control that normally comes from the --vmodule flag. Returns the previously effective level for that module pattern. Use this to raise/lower verbosity at runtime for specific modules (source-file name patterns).
requirements: module_pattern must be a valid, null-terminated C string specifying a --vmodule-style pattern (e.g., "my_module=2,foo*=3").
log_level is an integer verbosity level; higher values enable more verbose logs; 0 is the default.

If you need to change levels for VLOG sites that have already executed after/during InitGoogleLogging, you must supply the exact --vmodule pattern that applied to those sites; otherwise they will continue to be controlled by the level determined previously (often FLAGS_v).

Thread-safety and lifetime guarantees are not documented in this header; callers should avoid data races when changing levels concurrently with logging (unspecified behavior beyond benign race annotations on macro side).
Effect of this function may be limited or differ when building on compilers without GNU extensions where --vmodule functionality is not supported (per the header caveat).

functions.name: google::InitVLOG3__
functions.signature: extern GLOG_EXPORT bool InitVLOG3__(google::SiteFlag* site_flag, google::int32* site_default, const char* fname, google::int32 verbose_level);
functions.description: Internal helper used by VLOG_IS_ON to determine the controlling verbosity source for a logging site. It returns whether the given verbose_level is enabled for the file fname, and, when possible, sets fields in *site_flag (e.g., level pointer) so subsequent checks are fast. Not intended for direct use outside the logging infrastructure.
requirements: site_flag must be a non-null pointer to writable google::SiteFlag storage that persists for the lifetime of the logging site (typically a function-local static).
site_default must be a non-null pointer to an integer verbosity level to use as the default when no per-module override applies (commonly &FLAGS_v).
fname must be a valid, null-terminated C string naming the current source file (e.g., __FILE__).
verbose_level is the VLOG level being queried; it should be a non-negative integer consistent with VLOG conventions.

The function may update *site_flag; callers must ensure site_flag is not concurrently initialized by multiple threads without appropriate safeguards (the macro side uses benign race annotations; exact thread-safety guarantees are not documented here).

functions.name: AnnotateBenignRaceSized
functions.signature: extern "C" void AnnotateBenignRaceSized(const char* file, int line, const volatile void* mem, size_t size, const char* description);
functions.description: Marks a memory region as having a benign (intentional) data race for ThreadSanitizer (TSAN) reports. Intended for suppressing noisy race reports on specific memory (e.g., static variables) when building with thread sanitizer enabled. Typical usage is to pass source file and line (e.g., __FILE__, __LINE__), the address of the memory to annotate, its size in bytes, and a short description. Note: This declaration is only available when GLOG_SANITIZE_THREAD is defined; otherwise the function is not declared. Behavior and side effects are specific to TSAN; no runtime effect in non-TSAN builds.
requirements: Only call or reference this function when GLOG_SANITIZE_THREAD is defined (e.g., guard with #if defined(GLOG_SANITIZE_THREAD) or GLOG_IFDEF_THREAD_SANITIZER).
Parameter file should be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string representing a file path (commonly __FILE__).
Parameter line should be a non-negative source line number (commonly __LINE__).
Parameter mem must point to a valid memory region of at least size bytes; typically the address of a static/storage-duration object. The pointer may be volatile-qualified.
Parameter size specifies the number of bytes in the annotated region; must accurately reflect the memory region size and not exceed the accessible object size.
Parameter description should be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string describing the benign race (common usage); nullability is unknown.
Should be invoked before or at the time races on the target memory could be observed (commonly during static initialization or early startup).
The function does not return a value and does not report errors; callers should not expect error codes or exceptions.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets generic std::string inputs used across many glog stubs.
# Goals:
# - Provide varied but valid C-strings when consumed via c_str(): ensure a NUL terminator is present
#   implicitly by std::string (so avoid embedded NULs where APIs expect C-strings like filenames,
#   module patterns, email addresses). We still include some rare edge cases where NULs are acceptable
#   but keep them later in the sequence to not dominate.
# - Cover common shapes used by stubs: filenames/paths, module patterns, messages, email addresses,
#   program names, format fragments. Create a corpus mixture with reasonable lengths.
# - Keep total buffer <= 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded randomness for variability while reproducible under the given seed.
#
# Encoding format of the output buffer:
# We concatenate multiple strings separated by newline ("\n"). The fuzzer harness typically draws
# strings sequentially from the provided buffer. Newlines are safe delimiters and acceptable in most
# contexts when later truncated or sanitized by stubs. Each produced line avoids embedded NULs unless
# explicitly generating a case that can tolerate them.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"

def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, seq: str, length: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(r.choice(seq) for _ in range(length))

def _filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate plausible path or filename with extension used by stubs
    exts = [".cc", ".cpp", ".c", ".h", ".hpp", ".log", ".txt"]
    bases = ["main", "app", "module", "fatal", "errno", "to_string", "fuzz", "logger"]
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        # path form
        parts = []
        depth = r.randint(1, 3)
        for _ in range(depth):
            parts.append(_rand_choice(r, SAFE_CHARS, r.randint(3, 8)))
        base = r.choice(bases)
        ext = r.choice(exts)
        parts.append(base + ext)
        return "/" + "/".join(parts)
    else:
        base = r.choice(bases)
        ext = r.choice(exts)
        return base + ext

def _program_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    progs = ["fuzz_prog", "glog_fuzzer", "myapp", "svc", "daemon", "tool"]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return r.choice(progs)
    return _rand_choice(r, SAFE_CHARS, r.randint(3, 16))

def _module_pattern(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Only allow letters/digits/_/* per stub sanitation
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_*"
    s = _rand_choice(r, chars, r.randint(3, 16))
    # Occasionally start/end with wildcard
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        s = ("*" if r.random() < 0.5 else "") + s + ("*" if r.random() < 0.5 else "")
    return s

def _email_list(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Space- or comma-separated addresses
    domains = ["example.com", "test.org", "local", "example.net"]
    def one():
        local = _rand_choice(r, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "._+-", r.randint(3, 10))
        return f"{local}@{r.choice(domains)}"
    sep = ", " if r.random() < 0.5 else " "
    return sep.join(one() for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)))

def _message(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Human-readable message of bounded size
    words = ["hello", "world", "test", "logging", "info", "warning", "error", "fatal", "counter", "check", "errno", "syslog"]
    n = r.randint(3, 20)
    s = " ".join(r.choice(words) for _ in range(n))
    # Occasionally append numbers or small JSON-like payload
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        s += f" id={r.randint(0, 9999)}"
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        s += f" {{\"key\":\"{_rand_choice(r, string.ascii_lowercase, r.randint(3,8))}\"}}"
    return s[:512]

def _short_string(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = r.randint(0, max_len)
    chars = string.printable.replace("\x0b", "").replace("\x0c", "")
    s = _rand_choice(r, chars, length)
    # Avoid embedded NULs for C-string consumers
    return s.replace("\0", "")

def _symlink_basename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand_choice(r, string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.", r.randint(1, 32))

def _fingerprint(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand_choice(r, string.ascii_letters + string.digits, r.randint(6, 32))

def _subject(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = ["Status", "Report", "Alert", "Log", "Event", "Notice"]
    return f"{r.choice(base)} #{r.randint(1,9999)}"

def _vector_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # For operator<< on vector cases; we just provide a space-separated list
    tokens = [str(r.randint(-100, 100)) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 20))]
    return " ".join(tokens)

def _sanitize_for_filename(s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for c in s:
        if c in string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._-/":
            out.append(c)
        else:
            out.append('_')
    if not out:
        return "file.cc"
    return "".join(out)

def _corpus(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    items: List[str] = []
    # Program name for InitGoogleLogging
    items.append(_program_name(r))
    # Filenames/paths for various APIs
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        items.append(_filename(r))
    # Module patterns for SetVLOGLevel / InitVLOG3__
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        items.append(_module_pattern(r))
    # Messages of different sizes
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 6)):
        items.append(_message(r))
    # Email destinations and subjects/bodies
    items.append(_email_list(r))
    items.append(_subject(r))
    items.append(_short_string(r, 256))  # body-like
    # Symlink basename, log filename extensions
    items.append(_symlink_basename(r))
    items.append('.' + _rand_choice(r, string.ascii_lowercase, r.randint(1, 6)))  # extension
    # ToString/RawLog__ slices
    items.append(_short_string(r, 128))
    items.append(_short_string(r, 64))
    # Fingerprint
    items.append(_fingerprint(r))
    # Vector-like payload
    items.append(_vector_like(r))
    # A safe default filename if any consumer needs non-empty
    items.append("to_string.cc")
    # Add a couple of cleaned arbitrary strings to increase diversity
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        s = _short_string(r, 80)
        items.append(_sanitize_for_filename(s)) if r.random() < 0.3 else items.append(s)
    # Rare case: string with an embedded NUL for internal-only consumers; keep last
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        s = "nul_ok_" + _rand_choice(r, string.ascii_lowercase, 5)
        # Append visible \0 escape representation; actual NUL is avoided to not break C-string uses
        items.append(s)
    return items

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    items = _corpus(r)
    # Assemble with newlines, ensuring total size <= 4096
    data = "\n".join(items)
    b = data.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
        # Ensure we don't cut in the middle of a multibyte sequence: backtrack to last newline/ASCII
        try:
            b.decode('utf-8')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            # Trim to last safe boundary
            cut = len(b) - 1
            while cut > 0:
                try:
                    b[:cut].decode('utf-8')
                    b = b[:cut]
                    break
                except UnicodeDecodeError:
                    cut -= 1
    return b

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate a bytes buffer that will be used by the fuzzer runtime to
# supply values for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and integers.
# Target stubs use:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): needs a valid NUL-terminated filesystem path
#   pointing to random fuzzable data. We'll generate realistic paths and also
#   embed file-like content payloads separated in the buffer so the harness can
#   create files from them.
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): arbitrary strings; we generate printable and mixed data.
# - Various integers: we include some structured integer sequences to produce
#   interesting limits for TruncateLogFile (limit/keep) and RawLog__ printf args.
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit a small header indicating counts for paths, strings, and an optional
#   embedded file payload section.
# - Then emit sequences of NUL-terminated paths and strings.
# - Finally, emit a block of pseudo-random opaque bytes to serve as file data.
#
# The format is self-describing for the harness that consumes it; if the harness
# simply slices sequentially, the presence of many valid paths/strings still
# yields valid inputs. All strings are NUL-terminated, so any consumer that
# requires C-strings will work.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]

def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a mix of relative and absolute paths, with directories.
    parts_alnum = ''.join(sorted(set(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_-')))
    def rand_part():
        n = rng.randint(1, 12)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(parts_alnum) for _ in range(n))

    # Some special names and extensions
    specials = ["log", "tmp", "data", "stdout", "stderr", "app", "server", "client"]
    exts = ["", ".log", ".txt", ".dat", ".bin"]

    style = rng.randrange(6)
    if style == 0:
        # Absolute Unix-like
        depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
        parts = [rand_part() for _ in range(depth-1)] + [rand_part() or "file"]
        base = "/" + "/".join(parts)
    elif style == 1:
        # Relative path with directories
        depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
        parts = [rand_part() for _ in range(depth)]
        base = "/".join(parts)
    elif style == 2:
        # Current directory
        base = "./" + rand_part()
    elif style == 3:
        # Parent directory traversal (still valid path string)
        ups = "../" * rng.randint(1, 3)
        base = ups + rand_part()
    elif style == 4:
        # Hidden file
        base = "." + rand_part()
    else:
        # Named with special word
        base = _rand_choice(rng, specials) + "-" + rand_part()

    ext = _rand_choice(rng, exts)
    path = base + ext

    # Occasionally add a subdir for severity-based logs
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        sub = _rand_choice(rng, ["INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR"]).lower()
        path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), sub, os.path.basename(path))

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not path:
        path = "file.log"
    return path

def _rand_string(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix of printable, whitespace, percent signs (for printf-like strings), and some non-ASCII bytes encoded via latin-1 later.
    pools = [
        string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:/.",
        "[]{}()<>=,+-*#@!$%^&|~?",
        "\t\n\r",
    ]
    length = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    s = []
    for _ in range(length):
        pool = _rand_choice(rng, pools)
        ch = rng.choice(pool)
        s.append(ch)
    # Ensure some cases include percent sequences for RawLog__ formats
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and length < max_len - 2:
        s.append(" %")
        s.append(_rand_choice(rng, list("sdxluczp%")))
    return ''.join(s)

def _encode_cstr(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode using utf-8 but guarantee no embedded NULs; replace if any
    s = s.replace('\x00', '')
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    return b + b"\x00"

def _pack_u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Little-endian 32-bit unsigned
    n &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF, (n >> 16) & 0xFF, (n >> 24) & 0xFF))

def _gen_integers(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Provide a sequence of interesting 32-bit values for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) and others.
    ints: List[int] = []
    interesting = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023, 1024, 2047,
                   2048, 4095, 4096, 2**31-1, 2**31, 2**32-1]
    # Seed with interesting and random values
    ints.extend(interesting[: rng.randint(8, len(interesting))])
    for _ in range(rng.randint(16, 64)):
        ints.append(rng.getrandbits(32))
    # Shuffle
    rng.shuffle(ints)
    # Encode count then values
    out = _pack_u32(len(ints))
    for v in ints:
        out += _pack_u32(v)
    return out

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide counts, keeping under MAX_TOTAL.
    num_paths = rng.randint(1, 4)
    num_strs = rng.randint(2, 6)

    # Build header: magic + counts
    magic = b"GLG1"  # simple identifier
    out = bytearray()
    out += magic
    out += _pack_u32(num_paths)
    out += _pack_u32(num_strs)

    # Emit paths
    paths_bytes = bytearray()
    for _ in range(num_paths):
        p = _rand_filename(rng)
        paths_bytes += _encode_cstr(p)
    # Emit strings
    strs_bytes = bytearray()
    for _ in range(num_strs):
        max_len = rng.randint(8, 256)
        s = _rand_string(rng, max_len)
        strs_bytes += _encode_cstr(s)

    # Integers block
    ints_bytes = _gen_integers(rng)

    # Optional embedded file payload for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME data creation
    # Create a small realistic log content: lines with timestamps and severities
    def make_log_blob(max_size: int) -> bytes:
        severities = ["I", "W", "E"]
        lines: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 20)):
            sev = _rand_choice(rng, severities)
            pid = rng.randint(1, 65535)
            tid = rng.randint(1, 1_000_000)
            msg = _rand_string(rng, 80)
            lines.append(f"{sev}{rng.randint(0,12):02d}{rng.randint(0,59):02d} {pid} {tid} {msg}")
        blob = ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        return blob[:max_size]

    blob = make_log_blob(1024)

    # Assemble with section lengths
    def with_len(b: bytes) -> bytes:
        return _pack_u32(len(b)) + b

    out += with_len(paths_bytes)
    out += with_len(strs_bytes)
    out += with_len(ints_bytes)
    out += with_len(blob)

    # Ensure size bound
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])

import random
from typing import List

# Robust generator for opaque file data for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME consumers.
# Fixes previous bug: ensure randint ranges are valid even for small remaining sizes.

ASCII_SEVERITIES = [b"I", b"W", b"E"]


def _bounded_randint(r: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    # Returns a random int in [min(a,b), max(a,b)], inclusive.
    if a == b:
        return a
    if a > b:
        a, b = b, a
    return r.randint(a, b)


def _clamp(n: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    if n < lo:
        return lo
    if n > hi:
        return hi
    return n


def _make_ascii_log_lines(r: random.Random, approx_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    if approx_bytes <= 0:
        return b""
    counter = 0
    # Ensure we make progress even for very small approx_bytes
    target = max(approx_bytes, 1)
    while len(out) < target:
        sev = r.choice(ASCII_SEVERITIES)
        pid = _bounded_randint(r, 0, 99999)
        h = _bounded_randint(r, 0, 23)
        m = _bounded_randint(r, 0, 59)
        s = _bounded_randint(r, 0, 59)
        us = _bounded_randint(r, 0, 999999)
        filelen = _clamp(_bounded_randint(r, 3, 12), 1, 32)
        fname = bytes([r.choice(range(ord('a'), ord('z')+1)) for _ in range(filelen)]) + b".cc"
        line = _bounded_randint(r, 1, 2000)
        words = [b"hello", b"world", b"test", b"alpha", b"beta", b"gamma", b"delta"]
        msg_len = _clamp(_bounded_randint(r, 5, 60), 1, 200)
        msg = b" ".join(r.choice(words) for _ in range(_bounded_randint(r, 2, 6)))
        if len(msg) < msg_len:
            msg += bytes([r.choice(range(ord('a'), ord('z')+1)) for _ in range(msg_len - len(msg))])
        else:
            msg = msg[:msg_len]
        line_bytes = (sev + f"{pid:05d} ".encode() +
                      f"{h:02d}:{m:02d}:{s:02d}.{us:06d} ".encode() +
                      fname + b":" + str(line).encode() + b"] " +
                      msg + b" #" + str(counter).encode() + b"\n")
        # Ensure at least one byte gets added
        if not line_bytes:
            line_bytes = b"\n"
        out += line_bytes
        counter += 1
    return bytes(out[:approx_bytes])


def _make_binary_block(r: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    if size <= 0:
        return b""
    patterns: List[bytes] = []
    # Repeated single byte
    bval = _bounded_randint(r, 0, 255)
    rep_len = _clamp(_bounded_randint(r, 8, max(8, size // 4)), 0, size)
    patterns.append(bytes([bval]) * rep_len)
    # Alternating pattern
    a, b = _bounded_randint(r, 0, 255), _bounded_randint(r, 0, 255)
    alt_target = _clamp(_bounded_randint(r, 16, max(16, size // 3)), 0, max(0, size - sum(len(p) for p in patterns)))
    alt = bytearray()
    for i in range(alt_target):
        alt.append(a if i % 2 == 0 else b)
    patterns.append(bytes(alt))
    # Incrementing bytes
    start = _bounded_randint(r, 0, 255)
    inc_target = _clamp(_bounded_randint(r, 32, max(32, size // 2)), 0, max(0, size - sum(len(p) for p in patterns)))
    inc = bytes((start + i) % 256 for i in range(inc_target))
    patterns.append(inc)
    # Random noise to fill remainder
    used = sum(len(p) for p in patterns)
    noise_len = max(0, size - used)
    noise = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(noise_len))
    blob = b"".join(patterns) + noise
    return blob[:size]


def _compose_file(r: random.Random, target_size: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = max(0, target_size)

    # Header: ASCII log-like lines
    if remaining > 0:
        head_target = min(remaining, _clamp(_bounded_randint(r, 16, min(512, remaining)), 1, remaining))
        head = _make_ascii_log_lines(r, head_target)
        parts.append(head)
        remaining -= len(head)

    # Long line segment
    if remaining > 0:
        longlen = min(remaining, _clamp(_bounded_randint(r, 16, min(1024, remaining)), 1, remaining))
        # Decide whether to end with newline
        add_nl = (remaining > 1) and (r.random() < 0.3)
        if add_nl and longlen >= 1 and longlen <= remaining:
            long_line = b"L" * (longlen - 1) + b"\n"
        else:
            long_line = b"L" * longlen
        parts.append(long_line[:remaining])
        remaining -= len(parts[-1])

    # Binary block
    if remaining > 0:
        binlen = min(remaining, _clamp(_bounded_randint(r, 8, remaining), 1, remaining))
        parts.append(_make_binary_block(r, binlen))
        remaining -= len(parts[-1])

    # NUL block
    if remaining > 0:
        nul_len = min(remaining, _clamp(_bounded_randint(r, 0, min(128, remaining)), 0, remaining))
        parts.append(b"\x00" * nul_len)
        remaining -= nul_len

    # Tail ASCII if anything remains
    if remaining > 0:
        tail = _make_ascii_log_lines(r, remaining)
        parts.append(tail)
        remaining -= len(tail)

    data = b"".join(parts)
    # Optionally tweak final byte
    if data and data.endswith(b"\n") and r.random() < 0.5:
        data = data[:-1] + b"\r"
    return data[:target_size]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose size with safe bounds; always valid ranges
    size_candidates = [
        0,
        _bounded_randint(r, 1, 63),
        _bounded_randint(r, 64, 256),
        _bounded_randint(r, 257, 1024),
        1023,
        1024,
        _bounded_randint(r, 900, 1152),
        _bounded_randint(r, 1500, 2048),
        2047,
        2048,
        _bounded_randint(r, 2049, 3072),
        _bounded_randint(r, 3000, 4096),
    ]
    target_size = r.choice(size_candidates)

    data = _compose_file(r, target_size)

    # Optionally prepend/append small markers without exceeding 4096
    if r.random() < 0.5 and len(data) < 4096:
        marker = b"--logstart--\n"
        if len(marker) <= 4096 - len(data):
            data = marker + data
    if r.random() < 0.5 and len(data) < 4096:
        marker = b"\n--logend--\n"
        if len(marker) <= 4096 - len(data):
            data = data + marker

    return data[:4096]
